extracted.intended_audience: general readers of 19th-century travel/literary essays and social commentary
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from a 19th-century travel/essay narrative describing landscapes, social life, education, domestic life, and character ideals observed in the American Midwest. The passage mixes descriptive travel writing with prescriptive social views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education adapted to local needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction the children want to enable them to profit by the great natural advantages of their position; methods copied from the education of some English Lady Augusta are as ill suited to the daughter of an Illinois farmer as satin shoes to climb the Indian mounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish good schools near the community, planned by persons of sufficient thought to meet the wants of the place and time instead of copying New York or Boston methods. Education should prepare children to take advantage of local resources rather than rendering them useless at home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical choice of household musical instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: The guitar, or some portable instrument which requires less practice, and could be kept in tune by themselves, would be far more desirable for most of these ladies than the piano.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer portable instruments that require less practice and can be maintained by the household; avoid pianos in frontier homes because they are hard to keep in tune and often spoil the ear of inexperienced players.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of vocal and family-part singing
rubrics_metrics.description: Singing in parts is the most delightful family amusement, and those who are constantly together can learn to sing in perfect accord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After some elementary instruction, family and communal meetings (summer twilight, evening firelight) provide natural practice; prioritize good vocal music over elaborate instrumental performance in domestic settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical strength and practical skills for women
rubrics_metrics.description: If the little girls grow up strong, resolute, able to exert their faculties ... they would fit to enjoy and refine the Western farmer's life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Girls should develop bodily strength, dexterity, simple tastes, and practical resources to make home beautiful and comfortable; such preparation leads to greater happiness on the frontier than purely 'ornamental' accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of slavish imitation of European/Eastern standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Everywhere the fatal spirit of imitation, of reference to European standards, penetrates, and threatens to blight whatever of original growth might adorn the soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage original, locally-appropriate tastes and manners rather than mourning the absence of fashionable delicacy transplanted from Eastern cities; value native forms of elegance and adaptation to place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer local, uncomplicated domestic arts to city fashions
rubrics_metrics.description: An elegance [a frontier girl] would diffuse around her, if her mind were opened to appreciate elegance; it might be of a kind new, original, enchanting, as different from that of the city belle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate domestic arts and tastes suited to rural life rather than striving to reproduce metropolitan fashions that are impractical and mismatched to the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land stewardship and spaciousness over petty enclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A man need not here take a small slice from the landscape, and fence it in from the obtrusions of an uncongenial neighbor ... He can afford to leave some of it wild, and to carry out his own plans without obliterating those of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor larger, more open holdings and leaving portions of land wild rather than tight enclosure and minute, trivial 'improvements' that destroy natural character and limit enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospitality of the heart valued above material grandeur
rubrics_metrics.description: The hospitality of that house I may well call princely; it was the boundless hospitality of the heart, which, if it has no Aladdin's lamp to create a palace for the guest, does him still higher service by the freedom of its bounty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate hospitality by generosity of spirit and wholehearted welcome rather than by lavish material accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character qualities desirable in a national leader/man
rubrics_metrics.description: A man religious, virtuous, and--sagacious; a man of universal sympathies, but self-possessed; a man who knows the region of emotion, though he is not its slave ... who possesses prescience, as the wise man must, but not so far as to be driven mad to-day by the gift which discerns to-morrow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admire and seek leaders who combine moral seriousness, practical skill, broad sympathy, self-possession, and prudent foresight—neither dreamy idealists nor crude realists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty and alignment of public and private honor
rubrics_metrics.description: Would that the simple maxim, that honesty is the best policy, might be laid to heart; that a sense of the true aim of life might elevate the tone of politics and trade till public and private honor became identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote honesty as a guiding principle in civic and commercial life; evaluate public institutions and actors by their conformity to this moral standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sending daughters away to ill-suited schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Their grand ambition for their children is to send them to school in some Eastern city, the measure most likely to make them useless and unhappy at home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about sending rural daughters to urban Eastern schools whose methods and aims are unsuited to local life; prefer education that prepares them for the realities and advantages of their environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical judgement in choosing companions and guides
rubrics_metrics.description: I would not give [the bottle] to him, for I thought, if he got really drunk, there was an end to his services as a guide ... I fixed my eye steadily on his. He bore it for a moment, then his eye fell; he let go the bottle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise practical discernment and self-control in interactions (here illustrated in travel anecdotes); sound judgement and composure can be more effective than force or armament in managing difficult situations.
